question.prompt: The number \(25^{64} \cdot 64^{25}\) is the square of a positive integer \(N.\) In decimal representation, what is the sum of the digits of \(N?\)

solutions.explanation:
Both bases are squares, so taking the positive square root first makes the number easier to handle. Since \(25=5^2\) and \(64=8^2\),
\[
25^{64}\cdot64^{25}
=\left(5^{64}\cdot8^{25}\right)^2.
\]
Because \(N\) is positive, we have
\[
N=5^{64}\cdot8^{25}=5^{64}\cdot2^{75}.
\]
Each factor of \(5\) can pair with a factor of \(2\) to make \(10\). There are \(75-64=11\) factors of \(2\) left over, so
\[
N=2^{11}(2\cdot5)^{64}=2048\cdot10^{64}.
\]
Its decimal representation is \(2048\) followed by \(64\) zeros. Therefore its digit sum is
\[
2+0+4+8=\boxed{14},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Pair factors to make powers of ten
